evals.name: residency-boundary-aws-to-azure-tenant
evals.prompt: customer won't let any of their data leave their azure tenant, but we built everything on AWS/Bedrock. what actually has to move and what can stay?
evals.expected_output: Must identify that the model endpoint, the trace/observability store, AND the log destinations all sit inside the boundary — not just the app and database. Should name Azure AI Foundry as the in-tenant model endpoint, self-hosted tracing, and note that a SaaS trace store or vendor log aggregation breaks the clause. Should note the K8s core is what makes the move possible.

evals.name: prove-agent-cannot-exfiltrate
evals.prompt: we're on EKS calling Bedrock. security review is asking 'what stops the agent from sending data somewhere it shouldn't.' what do I actually show them?
evals.expected_output: Should give layered evidence: default-deny egress with PrivateLink/VPC endpoints (zero internet egress target), NetworkPolicies, DNS as an egress channel, S3 endpoint policy with aws:ResourceAccount, model-ARN allowlists in IAM+SCP+endpoint policy, and the audit surfaces that are OFF by default (invocation logging, CloudTrail data events). Bonus: the live kubectl curl-blocked demo.
